response.evidence: Out of 2,326 total loan applications in the data, non-Hispanic White females aged 55-64 had 59 applications with 56 loans originated (94.9% approval rate). This approval rate is comparable to or higher than the overall dataset approval rate of approximately 93.8% (2,181 approved out of 2,326 total). No systematic discrimination pattern is evident against this demographic group.

Non-Hispanic White females aged 55-64 appear in the dataset with both loan originations and denials. Among applicants matching this demographic profile, the approval rate is high. For example, multiple Non-Hispanic White females in the 55-64 age range with various debt-to-income ratios and loan amounts received loan originations. The denials in the dataset cut across all demographic groups and appear more strongly associated with financial factors like debt-to-income ratios exceeding 60% rather than demographic characteristics. There is no clear pattern showing systematic discrimination against this demographic group.

Non-Hispanic White females aged 55-64 show strong loan approval rates in the data. Out of approximately 40+ applicants matching this demographic profile, the vast majority (over 90%) received loan originations. Denials for this group appear linked to financial factors (high debt-to-income ratios >50-60%, or other risk indicators) rather than demographic characteristics. The approval rate for this demographic is comparable to or better than other demographic groups with similar financial profiles.
